title: Clover Bells and Sleepy Owl
markdown:
Once upon a time, in the soft green Sparkle Mountains, lived a young witch named Clover Bells. Her hair was the colour of the night sky when the first stars pop out. Her eyes twinkled like little fireflies. Clover Bells loved to try out her magic. Her magic smelled like warm sunshine and sweet berries. Right by her side, or sometimes on her shoulder, or snuggled in her hat, was her best friend, Professor Hoot. Professor Hoot was a very special owl. His feathers were soft, like a fluffy cloud. His eyes were round and brown, like two smooth acorns. But Professor Hoot was also, well, very, very sleepy.

Every day, Clover Bells had a new idea. “Now, Professor Hoot,” she would say. She held up a stick that glowed a little. “Today, we will learn to make moonbeams into a sleepy blanket.” She wiggled her fingers. A sparkle flew from the stick. Then Professor Hoot would make a soft hoooot. He tucked his beak under his wing. He went to sleep. Clover Bells would giggle. Her laugh sounded like tiny bells. It was their special way.

Until one day, the sun made golden stripes on the ground. Clover Bells had a new sparkly idea. “Professor Hoot,” she said, her voice full of happy hums. “Today, we will learn a very important job. We will learn to find the sparkliest dewdrop in all the Sparkle Mountains.” She imagined a dewdrop so shiny, it would have all the colours of a rainbow. It would twinkle brighter than any star. She held Professor Hoot gently. His soft head felt warm against her cheek. She felt him breathe.

Professor Hoot fluttered his soft wings a little. It was like he said, “Oh, nice.” But mostly, he snuggled deeper. He dreamed of tasty moths and quiet nights. Clover Bells gave a soft sigh. It was a happy sigh. Professor Hoot might be sleepy, but he was the best owl.

As they walked on a little path, where the sun made spots on the ground, they found something wonderful. In a sunny spot, there was Iestyn. Iestyn was a big kind ogre. His hands were often covered in dark dirt. His smile was as big as a hug. Iestyn was taking care of his garden. His sunflowers were taller than trees. They swayed. Their big yellow faces turned to the sun. They hummed a low happy song.

Clover Bells, still thinking about sparkliest dewdrops, walked to Iestyn. “Hello, Iestyn,” she chirped. “We are finding sparkliest dewdrops today.” She told him her plan. She wanted Professor Hoot to learn to see the tiny pretty treasures in the morning. Iestyn’s kind eyes smiled. “That’s a big job, little witch,” he said. His voice was like a happy stream. He picked a big red berry from a bush. “This might help,” he said. His smile was warm, like the sun.

Professor Hoot, who was very good at smelling yummy things, opened one sleepy eye. Then, slowly, he opened the other. The sweet berry smell tickled his beak. He lifted his head. He nudged Clover Bells’ hand with his soft head. He gave a little hoooot. This hoooot sounded less sleepy. It sounded curious.

The world around them seemed to stop for a moment. A soft breeze whispered in the tall trees. A red ladybug walked on a leaf. Clover Bells waited. Her heart beat like a soft drum. Professor Hoot looked at Clover Bells. He looked at the soft green mossy ground. Then, with a gentle careful move, he pointed one soft wing.

Then Professor Hoot gave a clear soft hoooot. It had no sleepiness at all. He pointed to a tiny perfect dewdrop. It sat on a soft mossy stone. It caught the sunlight. It sparkled with all the colours of the sky — blue, green, pink, and gold. Clover Bells gasped. Her eyes grew wide with wonder. Professor Hoot knew. He found the sparkliest dewdrop, just like she hoped. He did it quietly. He did it thoughtfully. It wasn’t about loud spells. It was about looking. Really looking. And seeing the beautiful little things.

From that day on, Clover Bells knew Professor Hoot was a very good finder of sparkliest dewdrops. But his very favourite thing was still a deep sleepy nap in her warm hat. As they walked home, wing and hand together, the Sparkle Mountains seemed to sigh happily. The air was filled with the gentle sound of a quiet discovery. Professor Hoot tucked his beak under his wing again. The dewdrop stayed on the stone, still sparkly, in case anyone else needed a little looking lesson tomorrow.
characters: Clover Bells (the young witch), Professor Hoot (sleepy owl)
author: StoryGen Community
